robot.name: ergoCub
robot.generation: ergoCub 1.0 with ergoCub 2.0 joint modules in development
robot.status_notes: Presented on 2023-09-21 at IIT's 20th-anniversary event in Genoa. Developed with INAIL as a research platform for ergonomic human-robot collaboration in industrial and hospital settings. Not for sale; no customer deployments found.
intended_use_cases: workplace ergonomics and physical risk reduction
collaborative payload lifting in industry and healthcare

height.notes: Official IIT announcement states 150 cm tall.

weight.notes: Official IIT announcement; also repeated by SteelReel.

payload.notes: SteelReel reports approximately 10 kg official load-bearing capability, but not necessarily an isolated max lift benchmark.

runtime.notes: No runtime was published in reviewed sources.

battery.notes: No public battery pack details found in reviewed sources.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Reported by emergentmind.com, added 2026-10-29 by automated spec fill; Partial scope only: the 17 DoF cited are the two 7-DoF arms plus the 3-DoF torso (upper body), not the robot's total-body degrees of freedom, which no supplied page states..

walking_speed.notes: No walking speed was published in reviewed sources.

hands.description: No detailed hand specification or hand DoF count found in reviewed sources.

items: Force Torque (F/T) sensors with inertial measurement units (IMUs)
Joint encoders, motor current sensors, F/T sensors, inertial sensors

compute.description: SteelReel AI reports onboard NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier and 11th-generation Intel Core i7; Wi-Fi 6E connectivity.

actuators.description: Compact, powerful joint modules were under development for ergoCub 2.0. No detailed actuator specifications found.

availability.notes: Research prototype; not for sale. No price or purchase path found.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: A peer-reviewed Nature Machine Intelligence figure shows ergoCub collaborating on a payload lifting task while adapting to a human partner; Emergent Mind describes 7-DoF arms plus 3-DoF torso control and hardware optimized for lifting. No fine-manipulation benchmarks or hand DoF were found.
caveats: No success rates or precision dexterity benchmarks.
No hand DoF or tactile fingertip specification found.
The 'heavy lifting' video is title-only and does not support detailed dexterity claims.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Autonomous warehouse navigation is reported only in simulation. WMF live demonstrations are stated to include live teleoperation and autonomy demonstrations, but control mode for individual videos is not verified. No real-world autonomous task execution evidence was found.
caveats: No independent autoload, intervention or success rate data.
Autonomy claims are directory or secondary reports, not verified.
Teleoperation status for most demos is not disclosed.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: The robot walked during a live demo on stage per a peer-reviewed figure and official IIT debut text mentions movement skills. Emergent Mind describes DNN-driven nonlinear MPC walking with step adjustment. No walking speed or fall data was published.
caveats: No walking speed, fall rate or disturbance-recovery metrics.
Videos are mostly title-only or secondary listings.
Teleoperation status for walking demos is unknown.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: F/T sensors with IMUs, Intel RealSense depth camera, LiDAR, and multimodal sensor fusion are reported. Emergent Mind summarizes perception and sensor fusion work. No independent perception benchmark was found.
caveats: Sensor list comes from a technical dossier and a figure caption, not measured specs.
No scene-understanding success rates or object recognition benchmarks.

human_interaction.summary: Human-aware collaboration is the core purpose. A peer-reviewed figure shows ergoCub monitoring a human's ergonomic state and adapting its motion during payload lifting. No quantitative HRI metrics were found.
caveats: No interaction questionnaires, safety studies, or worked-hours data.
Human ergonomic outcomes are described qualitatively.

endurance_reliability.summary: No battery capacity, runtime, endurance test, or reliability data were found in reviewed sources.
caveats: Complete absence of public endurance/reliability evidence.

human_environment_fit.summary: ergoCub is 150 cm tall, weighs 55.7 kg, and is designed for industrial and hospital collaborative tasks. No safety certification or human-proximity standard compliance was found.
caveats: No full-robot safety certification found.
Human-size and weight are official claims, not independently measured.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: ergoCub is a research prototype with no named customer deployment or commercial pilot found.
caveats: No customer sources or deployment metrics exist.

accessibility_value.summary: Not for sale. No price, lease, or purchase path found.
caveats: Research platform; public accessibility is not offered.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: ergoCub is a research humanoid from IIT/INAIL with a clear ergonomic human-robot collaboration purpose. The best public evidence is a peer-reviewed figure showing human-robot payload lifting and walking, plus official height/weight specs. However, there are no battery/runtime, total DoF, walking speed, price, or commercial deployment disclosures, and most detailed technical performance numbers come from secondary summaries.
strongest_positive_evidence: Peer-reviewed Nature Machine Intelligence figure documents human-robot collaboration and walking (iit-ergocub_evidence_006, iit-ergocub_evidence_007).
Official IIT announcement confirms 150 cm, 55.7 kg, and ergonomic workplace intent (iit-ergocub_evidence_001, iit-ergocub_evidence_002).
Secondary technical summaries describe up to 43% energy reduction and DNN-driven locomotion research (iit-ergocub_evidence_008, iit-ergocub_evidence_010).
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No battery capacity, runtime, walking speed, total DoF, hand DoF, or price.
No named customer deployment or independent verification.
Autonomy is simulation-only or title-only; no intervention logs or autonomous task execution evidence.
do_not_overclaim: Do not treat secondary summaries as independently verified research.
Do not claim commercial availability or customer deployment.
Do not infer total DoF from the 17-DoF arms+torso controller figure.
Do not describe video content beyond its title for unviewed YouTube sources.

currentness.currentness_notes: ergoCub is current as a research platform. ergoCub 2.0 joint modules were in development as of the reviewed sources, but no full successor release was found.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: ergoCub is IIT and INAIL's research humanoid, standing 150 cm tall, weighing 55.7 kg, and designed to reduce physical strain on workers in industrial and hospital settings. Its strongest evidence is a peer-reviewed Nature Machine Intelligence figure showing collaborative payload lifting with a human and live walking on stage. Official IIT sources confirm the 2023 debut and ergonomic purpose, while secondary dossiers report about 10 kg load-bearing, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier plus Intel i7 onboard compute, depth/LiDAR sensing, and research claims such as up to 43% energy reduction and DNN-driven locomotion. However, no battery, runtime, walking speed, total DoF, hand DoF, price, or customer deployment exists in the reviewed evidence; autonomy is mostly simulation-only or title-only.
strongest_evidence: Peer-reviewed figure documents human-robot payload lifting, ergonomic state monitoring, and walking (iit-ergocub_evidence_006, iit-ergocub_evidence_007).
Official IIT announcement confirms 150 cm, 55.7 kg, and ergonomic workplace intent (iit-ergocub_evidence_001, iit-ergocub_evidence_002).
Technical dossier and summaries report onboard compute, sensors, and optimization research (iit-ergocub_evidence_004, iit-ergocub_evidence_008).
weakest_evidence: No battery capacity, runtime, walking speed, total DoF, hand DoF, or price.
No customer deployment or independent verification.
Autonomous warehouse navigation is demonstrated only in simulation; live teleoperation/autonomy not verified.
known_do_not_credit: Do not credit unrelated AGIBOT, Unitree, or Figure videos from excluded sources.
Do not treat secondary research summaries as independent verification.
Do not claim commercial availability or customer deployment.
Do not infer total DoF from the 17-DoF arms+torso controller figure.
